profile.niche: Home workouts for busy office workers who want to get fit but can't make it to a gym
profile.audience: Home workouts for busy office workers who want to get fit but can't make it to a gym

research_material:
"I sit 9 hours a day, my back is destroyed, where do I even start"
"tried following gym youtubers but everything needs equipment I don't have"
"I get home at 8pm, cooking + workout + sleep is impossible, something has to go"
"do 10 minute workouts actually do anything or is that cope"
"started monday, stopped thursday, every single month, why am I like this"

pain_points: Chronic back pain from prolonged sitting with no idea how to address it
Lack of equipment at home makes following standard workout content feel inaccessible
Severe time scarcity—competing priorities (cooking, sleep, work) make fitting in workouts feel impossible
Skepticism about whether short workouts (10 min) are actually effective or just false hope
Chronic motivation failure—starting strong then quitting within days, repeating monthly

missing_info: Whether audience has tried any specific workout types (strength, cardio, stretching) or if pain/failure is universal across all approaches
What time of day works best for this audience (morning vs. evening vs. lunch break)
Whether the 'quit by Thursday' pattern is tied to specific workout length, intensity, or type
Competitor content that IS resonating (to avoid accidentally copying what's already working)

hooks.text: Most people think 8pm is too late. Here's what I do instead.
You don't need an hour at the gym. Seven minutes changes everything.
That tired excuse? Seven minutes just killed it.
Everyone says they're too busy. Watch what busy actually looks like.
Skip the gym guilt. This is what actually works.
Too exhausted after work? This changes your entire mindset.
Forget the 'no time' story. I'm about to prove it wrong.
Your 8pm is wasted potential. Here's the fix.
Nobody talks about the real workout that fits between dinner and bed.
Stop waiting for the perfect moment. Seven minutes is tonight.

winner.text: You don't need an hour at the gym. Seven minutes changes everything.
winner.reasoning: This hook directly dismantles the core barrier for your audience—time and gym access—while making a bold, credible promise. For busy office workers, 'seven minutes' is specific and believable, not hype. It positions the reel as a solution to their actual constraint, not motivation fluff.

runner_up.text: That tired excuse? Seven minutes just killed it.
runner_up.reasoning: Calls out the pain point directly with attitude that matches your casual voice. It's provocative enough to stop scrolls but safe because it's relatable rather than preachy. Works well if you want to lead with empathy-meets-accountability.

script.script:
[ON-SCREEN TEXT: You don't need an hour at the gym]

[HOOK - 0-3 sec]
You don't need an hour at the gym. Seven minutes changes everything.

[PAUSE]

[PROBLEM - 3-6 sec]
You're stuck at a desk. No time. No energy. Gyms feel impossible.

[CUT]

[VALUE - 6-25 sec]
Here's what seven minutes does:

[ON-SCREEN TEXT: Desk job killer workout]

Thirty seconds of burpees — your heart's pumping.

[PAUSE]

Thirty seconds rest.

Then jump squats. Push-ups. Mountain climbers. Repeat.

[ON-SCREEN TEXT: No equipment. No gym. Done before your next meeting.]

You'll feel stronger. More alert. Actually awake.

[CUT]

[CTA - 25-30 sec]
Do this three times a week. You'll notice the difference.

[PAUSE]

Follow for more seven-minute workouts that actually fit your life.
script.viewer_takeaway: Seven minutes of simple, no-equipment exercises can replace a full gym session and fit into a busy office worker's schedule with real, noticeable results.

cover_options: Split-screen: left side shows person slumped at desk, right side shows same person mid-burpee with energy/motion blur. Bold text overlay: '7 MIN > 1 HOUR'
Close-up of person's face looking tired at desk, with a pulsing heart-rate graphic and timer counting down from 7:00 overlaid. Text: 'Your desk job needs this'

frame_plan.on_screen_text: You don't need an hour at the gym
frame_plan.visual_direction: Person sitting slouched at desk, looking tired. Slow zoom on face. Graphic appears: red 'X' over gym/clock icon.
Cut to same person standing up with sudden energy. Bold gold text pops on screen. Quick beat of upbeat music spike.

frame_plan.on_screen_text: Stuck at desk. No time. No energy.
frame_plan.visual_direction: Quick cuts: clock ticking, person rubbing tired eyes, empty chair in office. Muted/grayed-out color grade.
Cut to bright, energetic setting (home/office corner). Person in workout position. Color grade returns to vibrant. Upbeat music starts.
Full-body shot of person performing burpees at fast pace. Show 3-4 reps. Close-up on movement. Heart-rate graphic pulses on bottom.
Person breathing, shaking out arms. Timer on screen counts down. Motivational visual: energy meter filling.
Quick clips of explosive jump squat reps. Show legs driving, landing soft. Dynamic camera angle (slightly tilted/active).
Close angle on push-ups. Show full range of motion. Cut between different angles to keep energy high.
Fast-paced mountain climber footage. Quick cuts between wide shot and close-up. Visual indicator (circle) shows 'repeat' animation.
Person finishing, slightly breathless, looking refreshed/energized. Transition back to desk/office setting. Show person looking alert/awake at computer.
Calendar graphic showing three workout days marked. Person looks noticeably stronger/more confident. Quick before/after energy visual.
Direct-to-camera or person pointing at camera with confident smile. Instagram follow button animation pops on screen. Upbeat music peaks.

assets_needed: B-roll: person at desk looking tired (close-up on face, wide shot of office)
B-roll: person performing burpees (3-4 reps, multiple angles)
B-roll: person performing jump squats (dynamic angles, full body visible)
B-roll: person performing push-ups (side angle, close-up)
B-roll: person performing mountain climbers (fast pace, multiple angles)
B-roll: person looking refreshed/alert after workout (desk setting transition)
Graphics: red X over gym/clock icons
On-screen text templates: casual, bold, gold/white color
Music: upbeat, high-energy track (start muted, build during hook, peak at CTA)
Optional: subtle whoosh/transition sound effects between exercises

justifications.clarity: Hook lands immediately with a direct comparison (7 min vs 1 hour) and the problem statement reinforces why this matters to the target audience.
justifications.retention: Energy shift from tired desk worker to movement keeps attention, but the middle section (exercise descriptions) relies heavily on b-roll pacing rather than narrative tension.
justifications.save_potential: Specific, actionable workout with no barriers to entry (no equipment, no gym) makes this highly bookmarkable for repeat reference.
justifications.shareability: Relatable pain point and time-efficient solution, but lacks a bold/surprising angle that makes people want to tag someone ('this is us').
justifications.audience_fit: Desk fatigue, time scarcity, and lack of gym access are directly addressed; the 3x/week cadence matches realistic office worker capacity.
justifications.cta_strength: Follow request is low-friction but passive; no urgency, exclusivity, or outcome promise attached to the follow action itself.

weaknesses.issue: CTA is generic and doesn't reinforce the benefit of following—it's a soft ask with no reason to act now.
weaknesses.fix: Replace 'Follow for more seven-minute workouts' with 'Follow for daily desk-killer workouts (takes less time than your coffee break)' or 'Follow for the workout series proven to beat desk fatigue by week 2.'

weaknesses.issue: Shareability underperforms because there's no social proof or identity element that makes viewers want to tag a friend or validate themselves.
weaknesses.fix: Add a line at 27-28 sec: 'Tag someone who's been saying they're too busy for the gym' or insert a subtle on-screen text at 21 sec: 'Your coworkers are already doing this' to create social proof and tagging incentive.

weaknesses.issue: Retention dips mid-video (6-21 sec) because the exercise montage is repetitive motion without narrative progression or motivation reinforcement.
weaknesses.fix: Rewrite the value section to include a micro-payoff: 'Thirty seconds of burpees—your brain clears. Thirty seconds rest. Jump squats—your legs fire back to life. Push-ups. Mountain climbers. Seven minutes. You go from desk-dead to actually awake.' This adds emotional arc instead of just listing moves.

captions: Your desk job is killing your energy. Seven minutes fixes it. This workout takes less time than a meeting—no gym, no excuses, just results. Do this 3x this week and tell me you don't feel different. Follow for more workouts that actually fit your life. 🔥

Can't make it to the gym? Neither can most of us. But seven minutes at your desk (or in your room) changes everything. Burpees. Jump squats. Push-ups. Mountain climbers. Repeat. No equipment. All energy. Try it three times this week—your afternoon self will thank you. Follow for the workouts busy people actually do.
growth.final_call_reason: Strong product-market fit and clear value, but CTA lacks urgency and mid-video retention sags due to exercise-listing monotony; rewrite the value section for emotional progression and attach a specific outcome or social hook to the follow request.
